changed.what: Applied H-verbs-5. sense.schedule's capability is sense:read (BD-258 rule). Its inputs are spelled as the VERBS-sense row spells them. --clocks <id>=<rate>,... Paging uses cursor, limit and follow, with 806 and 807. Added unit test schedule_inputs and an acceptance line. GATE-SENS-04 recording: the CPU part also holds KA-475/KA-476 of N20a-06, which depends on this bead (convention 7), and one receipt must cover the part (N38b-19). So this bead now writes no gate record; N20a-44 records the M1 part with record_gate from that receipt, in a session that did not implement the work (request to N20b-21).

sense.observability is a run verb (sense:run), so the M1 example now carries --key. --form linearized is the only M1 value; empirical and both answer 724 until BD-239. Scope said this bead records the KILL-EXPOSURE decision while Out gave it to N20a-27. Now this bead cites the outcome, and N20a-27 owns the ADR docs/adr/ADR-KILL-EXPOSURE-M2.md. GATE-SENS-06 is recorded by this bead (the register's measuring bead) with record_gate from its tests' receipt, not by N20a-45's script. The 1.05 ray-stage cost criterion had no test: added ray_stage_cost_ratio.

Scope said 'recording the KILL-SCHED decision', which contradicted item 7 (N20a-11 decides and records); it now says 'citing'. Named this bead as the register's measuring bead for the every-tier parts of GATE-SENS-04 and -05. Added the M2 completion of sense.schedule on every tier, which lifts the VERBS-sense row's form cpu restriction; N20a-44 already drives it with --tier.

The script's per-site rows used two filters, '-- KA-501 @strict', which would also select every other @strict entry. They now use the single entry filter KA-501@strict (N38a-02's id form). The sense.alias calls use BD-134's registered mission variants with distinct --key, in place of the unregistered --link shorthand.
The sense.observability calls the e2e script describes now carry distinct --key (a run verb, KNOWN_DRIFTS 5).

Named how GATE-SENS-09's measurement is split: BD-134 for the M1 docking rows, BD-240 for M3. Named the ADR path. The sense.alias calls it describes carry --key and the docking mission variants.

The S37 request was already satisfied: the e2e runs FROB_TEST_SEED=<seed> cargo test -p frob-conformance --test pilot_sched_race. Changed the Record item to N38a-09's schema. Path is crates/frob-conformance/registry/pilots.toml, schema frob.gauntlet.pilot/1. The id is PILOT-SENSE-<nn>, with gated_beads N20a-10. The protocol table carries blake3, frozen and ledger_seq; ceiling and fallback are tables with kill_gate KILL-SCHED; the tool is host. Results are appended as [[pilot.result]], with pass/falsified recorded as falsifier-rejected/falsifier-holds. The e2e reads the record read-only and checks the freeze date. Acceptance requires the record to validate.

The S37 request was already satisfied: stage 15 uses cargo test --test g3_metamorphic. The relation it named, 'same-instant-commute', is no registry row. The registered relation is MR-17 of relations.toml (N38a-17's row: referee/strict/lockstep, bits, mutation 'ordering by arrival'). The bead now binds its enumerator to MR-17 by identifier instead of registering a relation, filters '-- MR-17', and adds the dep N38a-17 (no cycle). Added unit test bound_to_mr_17 and MR-17's mutation as a negative control. The script's own spelling is asked of N20a-44.

Applied H-owners-1: the funding check is cargo run -p frob-conformance --example pilots -- fundable --bead N20a-10 / --package WP-40 --json. S37 was already met in substance (no frob gauntlet/gates command); the e2e now reads pilots.toml and gates.toml read-only, runs --test kill_sched_rule and N40-03's kill_gate_records.sh --live --ids, and asserts that fundable agrees with the outcome. The row gets a decision entry with outcome not-fired or fired; the status 'killed' is derived by apply_decisions, never written by hand. Added dep BD-095 for the frob evidence trace the script runs (no cycle).

Applied H-verbs-6: defined the sim.run input --intra-step hold|interpolate as new item 0. It applies to clocks the task does not declare, on lockstep batch-cpu, CUDA and Metal; interpolate holds consumer clocks. Precedence is task, then run, then profile default. The default is the OPEN-SENS-1 outcome (hold until decided). On the referee/strict profile it has no effect and the output says so. The resolved per-clock policies enter the RunId, and each clock's source is recorded; an unknown value is 802. Added an acceptance line and unit test intra_step_input. Script: every sim.run call has its own --key, and all arms run through sim.run (eval.run has no --intra-step). The unregistered 'frob fidelity ledger --against' is replaced by registered ledger, histogram (--against) and divergence calls plus this bead's decision example. ADR path is docs/adr/ADR-OPEN-SENS-1.md.

N20-KA now carries KA-512's tolerances and control, and KA-513's control, as '(set: N20a-14)'. The bead still called them proposed/to set; it now says set and registered (convention 12). The bias_initial_sigma draw, exposure averaging and card provenance were in scope but untested: added initial_bias_draw (10^4 episodes, 3% against a 0.7% spread), exposure_window_average and card_fields_provenance. The described sim.run calls carry --key. Arithmetic verified: 86.6 s, 156.96 m/s^2, the 16.1 g order mutant, 92 M samples.

Simulation time is rational, so no run ends at pi/2 s. A 50 ms odometry grid ends the arc at 1.55 s, which is about 21 mm and 21 mrad short of (1,1,pi/2), so the simulated arc check could not pass as written. The reference is now the closed form at the last odometry instant t_e (DESIGN: 10 ms on 400 Hz physics, t_e = 1.57 s, (0.99999968, 0.99920367) m). The Euler mutant check uses t_e = 1.55 s, where the mutant is 35 mm off (computed). Added unit test arc_closed_form_at_rational_end. Tolerances and controls are now 'set' per N20-KA. The described sim.run calls carry --key.

Applied H-ka-1: KA-523's tolerance is N20a-19's (1e-12 relative in double, 1e-4 in single; N38a-31 the same), not 1e-6. The point-sampling control (0.870/0.992/1.031 P at d = 2 mm, recomputed) still fails by far. Applied H-owners-1: --example pilots -- fundable --bead N20a-19 / --package WP-74. It now runs this bead's own target, --test pilot_tactile_arrays, and the mutant on that target. Oracle values re-verified (298.4 kPa, 2.969 mm, 1.452 N).

The S89 request was already satisfied: the pad pilot is N18b-35 (dep present, N38a-30 noted as superseded). The script never ran KA-523's G1 row, of which this bead is the owner; it now runs FROB_TEST_SEED=19 cargo test -p frob-conformance --test g1_known_answers -- KA-523 and asserts the row's tolerance. Run keys get a -<run-id> suffix, so a rerun of the script does not return an earlier stored receipt. Section 3 now says the registry carries the value as '(set: N20a-19)'.

requests.what: Name N20a-44 as the measuring bead of the M1 (CPU and referee) part of GATE-SENS-04, in place of BD-078. That part holds KA-471 to KA-476, and KA-475/KA-476 belong to N20a-06, which depends on BD-078. One record from one receipt covering all of the part's rows (N38b-19) can only come from a bead that depends on both. BD-189 stays the measuring bead for the every-tier part.

(1) Give each frob sim run call its own --key (sim.run is a run verb, KNOWN_DRIFTS 5). (2) Say who records GATE-SENS-04's M1 part: this bead, with cargo run -p frob-conformance --example record_gate -- --gate GATE-SENS-04 --receipt <hash> --part M1, from the G1 receipt covering KA-471 to KA-476, in a session that did not implement the work. The script never writes a gate record (convention 9). Acceptance line 64 is passive. (3) GATE-SENS-05's M1 part is BD-098's to record (N20b-21's register), not this script's: drop the referee/CPU recording clause for -05 or cite BD-098. (4) Stage 15's filter '-- same-instant-commute' names no registry row; use '-- MR-17', the relation N38a-17 registers and N20a-10 binds.
Give each frob sim run call its own --key. The script must not write the GATE-SENS-06 record: BD-188, the register's measuring bead, records it with record_gate from its receipt.

Give each frob sim run call (stages 2, 3, 6) its own --key. Stage 6's expected 'end pose (1, 1) m and pi/2' cannot be reached at a rational end time: compare with the closed form (sin t_e, 1 - cos t_e, t_e) at the run's last odometry instant t_e, which is 1.57 s on N20a-17's 10 ms grid.
Give each frob sense observability call its own --key (sense.observability is a run verb, sense:run).

Replace the unregistered --link late|on-time and --battery-m shorthands with BD-134's mission variants (--mission docking-late, --mission docking-on-time). Give every frob sense alias call its own --key.

The --intra-step hold|interpolate row is now defined by its owner N20a-12 (item 0), so drop 'requested'. Its Rules column could add what N20a-12 defines. The input applies to undeclared clocks on lockstep batch-cpu, CUDA and Metal, and interpolate holds consumer clocks. On the referee and strict profiles it changes nothing and the output says so. The resolved per-clock policies, not the raw input, enter the RunId.
